source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension / ASPIRE Project, IFAD-funded - "ដំណាំក្រូចថ្លុង" (Pomelo Cultivation Guide), 2017, 90pp
text:
For nursery-grown rootstock grafting (grafting onto seedling rootstock, ដើមគល់), rootstock seedlings are raised in nursery bags, commonly using a soil mix of roughly 70% topsoil with organic matter, 10% rice husk ash, and 10% river/coarse sand for good drainage, with beds or bag rows spaced to allow easy access for care.

Grafting is done once rootstock reaches a suitable diameter (finger thickness) at 15-20 cm above the growing medium; the source specifies checking that bark peels cleanly (confirming active sap flow) before making the graft cut. As with other citrus in this knowledge base, the graft union is wrapped tightly with plastic tape and checked after 2-3 weeks - a green, swelling bud indicates success, while a dry brown bud means the graft failed. After successful union and new growth, the rootstock top is cut back above the graft to force growth into the new scion, and grafted plants are grown on in the nursery before field planting, spaced roughly 15 x 20 cm apart in nursery beds.
